# Standard Compute Overview
Source: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/standard-overview
Fetched: 2026-06-16
Last updated on page: October 7, 2025

## What is standard compute?
"Standard compute is compute configured with standard access mode. Standard compute resources can be used by any user given permission to do so."
"Standard compute allows any number of users to attach and concurrently execute workloads on the same compute resource."
"Standard compute is recommended for most workloads" — allows any number of users to attach and concurrently execute workloads, "providing cost savings and simplified compute management."

## Access mode selection
Access mode configured in Advanced section during compute creation.
API field: `data_security_mode`
Default: Auto — automatically chosen based on selected Databricks Runtime.
"Auto defaults to Standard unless a machine learning runtime or a Databricks Runtimes lower than 14.3 is selected, in which case Dedicated is used."

## When to use standard compute
- General data engineering and ETL pipelines
- Collaborative data science projects
- Interactive data exploration
- Cost optimization
"Choose dedicated compute only for specialized workloads requiring privileged machine access, RDD APIs, distributed ML, GPUs, or R."

## Language and runtime support
- Python: Full support for all Databricks Runtime versions
- SQL: Full support for all Databricks Runtime versions
- Scala: Supported on Databricks Runtime 13.3 LTS and above with Unity Catalog
- R: Not supported on standard compute

## Lakeguard for user isolation
"Standard compute uses Databricks Lakeguard to provide secure user isolation and data governance."
"Uses advanced code isolation techniques that separate user code from the underlying Spark infrastructure."
